## Executive Summary

- OpenAI introduced a broad set of new agent-facing products in 2026, including three real-time audio models (GPT-Realtime-2, GPT-Realtime-Translate, GPT-Realtime-Whisper), the GPT-Live voice framework, the GPT-5.6 tiered model family (Sol, Terra, Luna), and the OpenAI Presence enterprise agent platform.
- Codex underwent major changes: token-based credit billing (April 2), native image generation via GPT Image 2 (April 21), and a preview system that generates 2–4 implementation approaches; OpenAI estimates power-user spend at roughly $100–200 per developer per month.
- By June 2026, Codex had become the primary AI tool across every OpenAI department; median internal use in Research rose 56x versus November 2025, with notable increases in Customer Support (32x), Engineering (27x), and Legal (13x).
- OpenAI deepened its ecosystem and enterprise work through the OpenAI Partner Network (June 14), a $150M ecosystem investment, and a strategic collaboration with Accenture Federal Services for U.S. federal agencies.
- Governance and lifecycle activity included the Frontier Governance Framework (May 28), the launch of Rosalind Biodefense, the wind-down of Agent Builder and Evals, and a qualified external report that OpenAI’s roadmap includes AI research interns by 2026 and AGI researchers by 2028.

### New voice and real-time audio models

OpenAI introduced three real-time audio models for AI agents: **GPT-Realtime-2**, **GPT-Realtime-Translate**, and **GPT-Realtime-Whisper**. Separately, OpenAI introduced **GPT-Live**, a new generation of voice models for natural human-AI interaction, now powering ChatGPT Voice; it is described as a new framework for voice interaction. OpenAI will continue supporting voice customers with access to frontier models through the OpenAI API.
